text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's The Ass in the Tiger-Skin; the frame is stated correctly: the monkey tells it to the crocodile in Book IV.

The laundryman's trade is dropped as a caste label and disclosed; he is simply ಬಡವ. A false 'kept' claim about cloth bundles was corrected to 'added' before approval, and the man now fetches the donkey home before dawn in scene 4 as in Ryder and scene 3.

Age band 10+: the disguised crop-raider is killed with sticks and stones, told in one plain sentence; the arrows and the dead tiger's body are omitted with disclosure. The content note says plainly that the donkey is beaten to death.
The pause question comes before the bray; the donkey is in the neuter; no em dashes.

The thin grey donkey with ribs showing in panel 1 becomes round and plump in panels 4 and 5. The tiger skin is a flat striped hide with no head, claws or blood, draped so the donkey's head, legs and tail stay visible.

The two farmers peep from behind the fence in panel 3 and stand up in surprise with a clay oil lamp in panel 5; panel 6 shows only the man with an empty rope at the empty shed. The beating and the death are not drawn.
No caste markers or modern objects. One whole-sheet edit pass removed a brownish fade at the panel edges, keeping the composition; the credit line says so.
